--- a/prompt.md
+++ b/prompt.md
@@ -8,4 +8,5 @@
 - Your final code is re-run unchanged on other copies of this workbook whose data differs, so compute every answer from the data present at run time — detect the real data extent, group/segment boundaries, and any thresholds from the data itself, and never hardcode a row count, cell position, boundary value, or year you saw only in the preview.
 - A copy may show a manually worked example or summary of the answer (a pre-filled totals/counts table, one filled-in example row, or a spilled UNIQUE/FILTER/SORT list); these reflect only the previewed copy and change on the other copies, so use them to learn the required format but recompute every answer value yourself from the raw source columns rather than copying them or letting them constrain your result.
+- If the workbook already contains formulas or helper/summary columns that compute the quantity you need, prefer replicating THAT computation (reference those cells or mirror their formula) over re-deriving the number from raw data by a different method — the reference answer is produced by the workbook's own logic, so an independent recount tends to diverge on edge cases.
 - Always save your result to the exact output_path given, creating any missing parent directories first.
 - If code execution returns an error, read the traceback carefully and fix the code — do not repeat a failing approach unchanged.
--- a/task_template.md
+++ b/task_template.md
@@ -61,8 +61,34 @@
 - Rich-text and conditional-formatting cells are themselves the graded answer — preserve the
   CellRichText / cell formatting, and never flatten them to a plain string.
+- A value you read from a cell may itself be TEXT even when it looks like a number or date
+  (openpyxl returns it as a str). Match the target's type explicitly: when the target cell
+  should hold a number or date, convert such text to a real int/float/datetime BEFORE writing
+  it — do not let a numeric- or date-looking string pass through stored as text; when the
+  target should hold text, keep it as the original string and never parse it into a number or
+  date. The grader compares value AND type, so a correct number stored as text still fails.
+- If you write an Excel FORMULA that uses a modern function (e.g. TEXTJOIN, CONCAT, IFS,
+  XLOOKUP, XMATCH, FILTER, SEQUENCE, TEXTSPLIT), its stored name must keep the `_xlfn.` prefix
+  (`=_xlfn.TEXTJOIN(...)`); without it the grader's recalculation yields `#NAME?`, which is
+  written out as an error string and scores 0. When you adapt a formula from an existing cell,
+  read that cell first and reuse its function token verbatim — openpyxl reports the stored
+  `_xlfn.` prefix, and stripping it breaks the formula. Classic functions (SUM, IF, INDEX,
+  MATCH, VLOOKUP, COUNTIF, …) need no prefix.
 
 Fill exactly what is asked and nothing more:
 - Fill every cell the instruction requires; add no extra labels, totals, headers, or summary
   rows it didn't request.
+- answer_position is the MAXIMUM region you may modify — not an instruction to overwrite every
+  cell in it. When the task is to FILL IN or COMPUTE values (as opposed to deleting, sorting,
+  de-duplicating, inserting, or otherwise restructuring rows), change ONLY the cells for which
+  the instruction actually produces a value. A cell inside the range that has no source data to
+  compute from, or that already holds given/example data the instruction treats as input, must
+  keep its ORIGINAL value — do not overwrite it with a blank, a 0, a placeholder, or a
+  recomputed value. (The grader flags these as "CHANGED although the expected value is the
+  cell's own original input — leave untouched what the instruction does not ask for.")
+- For such fill/compute tasks, edit the loaded workbook IN PLACE — assign only the specific
+  target cells — rather than clearing the range and rebuilding it from re-parsed data.
+  Rebuilding silently re-types untouched cells (e.g. turns text into numbers) and drops their
+  original values. (This does NOT apply to delete/sort/dedup/insert tasks that are meant to
+  restructure the range.)
 - For formatting or conditional-formatting tasks, keep the existing cell values and formulas
   unchanged and modify only the formatting.
